headline: Japanese builder Shimizu has invested in Noble Machines, a California humanoid robot startup, and launched a joint effort to develop robots for construction sites.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a named industry investor and a plan with dates, but no investment amount and no real-site test yet.
importance_line: Construction workers in dangerous jobs, and builders short of staff, are the target, but the robots are still at the simulation stage and real-site tests do not start until next spring.
summary: AI Insider reports, citing Shimizu, that the Japanese construction company has invested in Noble Machines, a Sunnyvale, California, startup founded in May 2024, to develop humanoid robots that could assist with or replace workers in hard and hazardous tasks such as moving materials, navigating sites and patrols. Computer simulations are due to start by the end of this year and tests on real construction sites next spring, and Shimizu says an aging workforce and fewer young entrants are squeezing the industry.
notes: Funding and partnership item: robots are still in development, none shown working yet. Investment amount not stated.
